cited_not_verified: w0 = -tau for E6 (w0 the longest Weyl element)
-1 in W  <=>  every representation is self-dual
the outer involutions of e6 are exactly tau up to inner automorphism
the_mechanism: tau != id is EQUIVALENT to the 27 being complex (via w0 = -tau, so -1 not in W, so complex reps exist); and tau is the ONLY involution that can reduce rank (all inner ones fix the full Cartan). One structure, two roles: spending it on rank lands in Fix(tau), where 27 = 27bar

why_not.no_conjugate_pair: one object with two roles, not two non-commuting observables
why_not.no_quantitative_bound: a dichotomy, not a trade-off curve; no rank-5 half-chiral state
why_not.not_simultaneously_meaningful: the outcomes are mutually exclusive, not jointly blurred
why_not.no_state_space: nothing on which a variance could be measured
why_not.reality_type_is_discrete: Frobenius-Schur +1/-1/0 -- there is no continuous amount of chirality

THE_SCOPE_CORRECTION.what_B576_actually_supports: along any integrable deformation OF THE GEOMETRIC REPRESENTATION with nonzero theta-odd component, the Zariski closure is forced to full E6(C) -- the mechanism being the block-sum lemma, which works because such deformations CONTAIN THE PRINCIPAL sl2 (its centralizer in e6 is zero, blocks multiplicity one)
NOT_established_for: arbitrary representations of pi_1 into E6
FINITE-image representations (A4, D5, S5) -- which contain no principal sl2
THE_SCOPE_CORRECTION.why: the finite-image case is closed INDEPENDENTLY by B959's torality argument (elementary abelian rank <= 2 => toral => rank 6), not by the threshold; so the no-go stands, but the UNIFIED 'no intermediate regime' framing does not
